title: Samsung is building a private AI cloud that could make Galaxy AI far more powerful
excerpt: Samsung's private cloud server would allow for anonymous and secure AI-processing.
content_html:
Published Nov 26, 2026, 11:01 AM EST

Mark has been covering smart devices for the better part of a decade now. He wrote over a thousand articles for Digital Trends and worked as an editor there, before moving to Android Police in 2025.

He's written about everything from budget phones to flagship phones, e-readers, smartwatches, fitness trackers, and anything else that might connect to a smartphone in some way. 

Starting his mobile tech career with accessory seller Mobile Fun, he's unusually obsessed with stuff that clips onto or connects to phones, and he loves it when a new accessory lands on his desk.

He worked for Digital Trends from 2017 to 2025.

Samsung is allegedly building a private AI cloud that would allow for cloud-processing of AI data, while keeping it completely anonymous.

This would bypass many of the privacy concerns around using a cloud-based AI, and it would follow in the footsteps of companies like Apple and Google. It may also allow Samsung to take some big additional steps with Galaxy AI.

Samsung's private AI cloud is called SPAC

Completely anonymous and encrypted

Some AI features run well enough on your phone, granted you have powerful enough hardware. But for some tasks, an on-device AI model simply isn't enough, and data needs to be sent to a company's cloud server for processing.

This is the difference between on-device AI and cloud-based AI, and the power available for processing isn't the only difference between the two.

Since using on-device AI doesn't involve any intermediaries, it's seen as the more private of the two options. Cloud-based AI, on the other hand, is seen as much less safe for your privacy. Your data is sent to a server and back again, after all. So if you're the sort of person who's careful about what data they allow out of their grip, cloud-based AI is a no-no.

According to exclusive reporting from Android Authority, Samsung is looking to change that by creating its own private AI cloud that users could access without revealing any personal details.

This is exactly the same tech we've seen from Apple, Google, and even Meta in the last few years. According to code discovered in the latest One UI 9.5 Beta 1, this cloud is currently known as "SPAC", and it seems to be focused heavily on privacy.

Android Authority claims that code in Photo Editor, IntelliVoiceService (Samsung’s speech and language service), Smart Capture, and PhotoRemasterService make reference to SPAC. Importantly, there was no mention of this in these apps' coding prior to this beta, so this is a very new service. Unfortunately, none of them can use it yet, indicating the server is off.

As mentioned, SPAC is very much about providing heavy privacy. It uses a third-party relay, so Samsung only knows what's being asked for, and not who asked for it. Your phone and Samsung's servers will also swap authentication, to prove Samsung's servers are genuine, and that you're a real Galaxy AI user. It will also contain some form of record that can't be altered.

SPAC could be exceptionally important for Galaxy AI. If Samsung is able to send more processes to the cloud without user privacy concerns, then the amount of power available is increased. That means more capable and faster AI models can be made available, which could be a huge benefit for the Galaxy AI Premium subscription.

At this time, there isn't much more to go on other than the fact SPAC exists, and that Samsung is working on it. There's certainly no indication it's a finished product, and it's possible it never comes to fruition. That is likely to be the case if the AI bubble bursts any time soon.
